notes:
CURRENT STATUS: blocked. The following author narrative predates the independent review; any historical stop or safe-state claim in it was withdrawn by that review. The regenerated references now match the current no-native-stop definition.

Gate run: G1, G2, G3, G4, G5, G6, G8 and G9 pass; G7 warn with only G7.LEGACY_SOURCE (liquidhandler.py is Python 2; the gate read it with 12 lines Python 3 cannot parse left out). There are no G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warnings. Hardware was never attached and the hardware backend was never run. This package is model-authored and unreviewed; driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null and the loader refuses its R2 hardware backend until a human signs it.

Risk is R2, above the card floor R0, because the device is a liquid handler with a robot arm and a syringe pump that dispenses (MHS-004 section 2.1). The clone documents no independent hardware e-stop and no stop or halt command at all (Protocol.md:55-65). The safe-state action x-cap.dwinters42.stop_pump.v1 and the @estop method command every syringe pump to zero speed at its tracked position through the native Pump method; speed 0 is inside the native check (liquidhandler.py:132-134) although the protocol text states 1 to 20 for operator commands (Protocol.md:64). The runtime latch refuses later commands. NOT COVERED: there is no physical arm stop and no independent hardware e-stop, so no such protection is claimed. The actions expose device steps and uncalibrated syringe units, not uL or mm, because the clone states no conversion. NOT COVERED: Goto, SaveLocations and LoadLocations are not exposed as actions. The fake is an in-memory stand-in, not a recording; its arm limits, one pump and 1000-unit starting volume are placeholders, and the read arrays are small (three coordinates, one syringe). The hardware factory native.py is a Python 3 port of the documented framed serial protocol, because the clone cannot be imported under Python 3; it carries the upstream copyright and permission notice, and it needs pyserial, which the card install block does not list. It was not run. The clone header is an ISC-style permission text while setup.py says BSD; the card records license_spdx NOASSERTION, and this package claims no other licence. site-limits.example.json is an example overlay, not a statement about any unit: its 2000 units, 2500/1000/1200 steps, two arms and one pump are operator examples, and an operator must issue site-limits.json for the actual instrument. The 1 to 20 speed limit is the only sourced numeric bound; the arm travel, syringe volume, pump position and arm/pump/axis counts are operator_required.
